title: Axeyum claim ledger record
description: One mathematical claim as a first-class artifact joining the knowledge graph (concepts, prerequisites, epistemic status) to machine-checked evidence (witnesses, certificates, checkers). Untrusted search proposes; recorded checkers dispose. A claim's epistemic_status uses the math-education vocabulary verbatim so the two corpora share one epistemics.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identity; equals the containing directory name.

statement.description: The claim in one or two precise human sentences, including quantifier ranges. This is what the evidence is evidence FOR.

epistemic_status.description: math-education graph/vocab semantics, verbatim: axiom=assumed; proved=general-case proof; computed=established by calculation or exhaustive check over a stated range; empirical=observed; conjectured=believed, unproved; open=nobody knows.

language.description: How the claim is mechanized. cnf-family: a parameterized generator emits the deciding CNF. prose-only claims cannot carry checked evidence.

family.description: Generator or theory family, e.g. 'rado-colouring-a(x-y)=bz'. One family = one semantics note + one generator.

parameters.description: Exact instantiation, e.g. {"a":2,"b":3,"k":4,"n":225}. The generator plus these parameters must reproduce the deciding instance bit-for-bit.

generator.description: Repo-relative path of the instance generator.

semantics_note.description: Repo-relative path documenting the encoding's faithfulness argument.

concept_refs.description: Anchors into the math-education knowledge graph. Follows that repo's resolution policy: a ref may be pending (target not yet written) but a pending ref must never be asserted as resolved, and a release gate requires resolution or removal.

ref.description: A concept (C:slug), encounter (C:slug@level), misconception (M:slug), technique (TQ:slug), thread or theme id.

relation.description: instance-of: the claim instantiates the concept. exercises: deciding it exercises the concept at that encounter depth. refutes: machine evidence against a misconception. frontier-of: the claim sits on the open frontier of the concept. uses-technique: the proof/search uses the technique.

resolved.description: True only if the target id exists in the pinned graph snapshot named by provenance.graph_pin.

fragments.description: smt-fragments.json row ids exercised by the deciding route, e.g. ["qf_bv"]; empty if decided outside axeyum.

scenario_family.description: axeyum_scenarios::Family variant realizing this claim as a self-checking exercise, when one exists.

searched_by.description: UNTRUSTED search tools with versions, e.g. 'kissat 4.0.4', 'lsearch (min-conflicts, seed 12345)'. Nothing here is in the trust base.

checked_by.description: TRUSTED disposers with versions: independent verifiers, certificate checkers. Every definitive evidence row names at least one.

toolchain.description: Pinned identity of the software that produced regenerable evidence. REQUIRED whenever any evidence row carries a `regeneration` block: a recipe without a pinned toolchain is not reproducible, because a different build produces a different artifact and the recorded hash becomes unfalsifiable.

axeyum_commit.description: 40-hex commit of this repository at build time.

dirty.description: True if the working tree had uncommitted changes at build time. A dirty build cannot be reproduced from the commit alone, so a regenerable evidence row built dirty is recorded honestly rather than silently.

graph_pin.description: 40-hex commit of the math-education repo against which concept_refs.resolved was evaluated.

establishes.description: Exactly what the cited work establishes, so our delta is auditable.

evidence.description: Machine-checked evidence rows. A claim with epistemic_status 'computed' must carry at least one row whose check_status is 'checked'. Rows are append-preferred; superseded rows keep history.

kind.description: witness-replay: a concrete object re-validated against the definition. unsat-certificate: DRAT/LRAT/Farkas artifact re-checked by an independent checker. cube-cover: a decomposed refutation — every cube of an exhaustive case split independently refuted and its proof checked; the artifact is the per-cube ledger and the checker re-verifies exhaustiveness against the formula's own case-split clauses. exhaustive-enumeration: full finite sweep. published-value-replication: our pipeline reproduces a cited value. bound-citation: a bound taken from literature, NOT machine-checked here.

parameters.description: Evidence-row-specific parameters the checker needs, e.g. {"branch": [2,4,6,8], "cubes": 256} for a cube-cover.

supports.description: The exact sub-statement this row supports, e.g. 'R_4 > 240 (lower bound)'.

artifact.description: Repo-relative path of the evidence artifact (colouring, DRAT file, log).

regeneration.description: For evidence too large to distribute: the exact command that reproduces the artifact and the SHA-256 of what it produces. Because checking a proof costs orders of magnitude more than regenerating it, a recipe plus a hash imposes almost no extra cost on a verifier while removing gigabytes from the record. Requires provenance.toolchain.

command.description: Exact, runnable command producing the artifact.

check_status.description: checked: an independent checker validated the artifact and the run is recorded. replay-only: re-derived but not by an independent tool. not-checked: recorded, no machine validation (mandatory for bound-citation).

checker_command.description: Exact reproduction command, or 'none' for bound-citation rows.

artifact_format.description: Dialect of the stored artifact, read from its BYTES by the validator and never taken from this record's say-so (findings register B8).

distribution.description: Set by a bundle builder on rows whose artifact that bundle deliberately does not carry. The row must still record artifact_sha256, so what regeneration has to produce stays pinned. Never set in the ledger itself.

frontier.description: Present iff epistemic_status is 'conjectured' or 'open': what is known and what would settle it. This is the field that makes open problems first-class instead of unrepresentable.

known.description: Current best bounds/partial results with their evidence ids or citations.

would_settle.description: The concrete artifact that would settle the claim, e.g. 'an UNSAT certificate for F_n at any n, plus a verified colouring at n-1'.

supersedes.description: Claim id this record supersedes (e.g. a strictly better bound).
